changes.change: Success response code changed from 201 to 200 for 'Order created'.
changes.why: Clients and generated SDKs that expect 201 (or a typed 201 response) will not match a 200 response; status-code checks fail.

changes.change: The whole PUT operation was removed from the path.
changes.where: spec/paths/orders-id.yml (put block removed; formerly origin/main lines 17-43)
changes.why: Existing callers of PUT /orders/{orderId} get 404/405 and the generated updateOrder method disappears from SDKs.

changes.change: New required request property 'currency' (type string) added to CreateOrder.
changes.why: Requests that were valid without currency are now rejected by strict validation; generated createOrder request type gains a required field.

changes.change: 'quoteDate' removed from the required list; the property remains, optional.
changes.endpoint: Order schema (used by GET /orders/{orderId}, POST /orders response, POST /orders/search items)
changes.why: Clients that rely on quoteDate always being present may now receive it absent; generated types change from required to optional, which breaks strictly typed consumers.

changes.change: Order.amount meaning changed from major units (e.g. 12.50) to minor units/cents (e.g. 1250). Type stays number.
changes.where: spec/schemas/Order.yml:17 (was 'The total in major units, e.g. 12.50')
changes.why: Same field, same type, but values are 100x larger; clients that read or display the amount as major units will misreport totals silently.

changes.change: Enum value ROLLBACK removed from OrderStatus.
changes.endpoint: GET /orders/{orderId}, POST /orders (request status and response), POST /orders/search (statuses filter and items)
changes.why: Responses carrying ROLLBACK no longer match the enum, and generated enums lose the variant (exhaustive switches break); requests that send status ROLLBACK (e.g. a search filter) are now rejected by validation.

changes.change: 'limit' type changed from number to string with maxLength 3.
changes.why: A request with a numeric limit (e.g. 50) that was valid is now rejected; generated type changes from number to string. Limits longer than 3 characters are also rejected.

changes.change: Result ordering reversed: items are now sorted oldest-first by createdAt instead of newest-first.
changes.why: Same request returns the same items in reverse order; clients that take the first item as the latest will get different data. The spec does not document ordering.

changes.change: 'skip' changed meaning: it was an item offset and is now a page index, so the slice offset is skip * limit.
changes.why: The same skip value returns a different page: e.g. skip=1 with limit=10 previously skipped 1 item and now skips 10; pagination loops built on skip break. The spec gives no description for skip, so the change is invisible in the contract.

Requests with 'before' no longer satisfy the required 'from' parameter and are rejected; generated method signature changes. The meaning of 'from' is not described, so clients cannot assume it equals the old bound.

changes.change: Query parameter 'top' changed from optional to required (its default of 10 is now unreachable without sending it).
changes.why: Calls that omit 'top' (valid before, using default 10) are now rejected; generated method gains a required argument.

changes.change: Query parameter 'before' boundary changed from exclusive to inclusive.
changes.where: spec/paths/stats-charts.yml:8 (was 'The end of the period, exclusive')
changes.why: The same call now includes records created exactly at 'before', so counts and chart points change for identical requests.

changes.change: New optional query parameter 'currency' (type string) added.
changes.why: Optional addition; existing calls remain valid and unchanged. The repo does not contain the chart code, so the filter's effect could not be verified.

changes.change: Operation summary reworded from 'Receive an order by id' to 'Get one order by its id'.
changes.why: Wording only; the meaning and contract are unchanged (only generated doc comments differ).

changes.endpoint: Order schema (GET /orders/{orderId}, POST /orders response, POST /orders/search items)
changes.why: Purely additive optional response field; clients that ignore unknown fields are unaffected.
